errata.note: Article IX split into its four parts (IX-A Common Provisions, IX-B Civil Service Commission, IX-C Commission on Elections, IX-D Commission on Audit); part headings that the source left at the end of sections removed from the section text. Art. VI, Secs. 29–32 relabelled.

Outdated text in the source. RA 9244 (2004) abolished the preparatory recall assembly. Recall now starts only by a petition of registered voters: at least 25% where the voting population is 20,000 or less; 20% (minimum 5,000) up to 75,000; 15% (minimum 15,000) up to 300,000; 10% (minimum 45,000) above 300,000. COMELEC certifies the sufficiency of signatures within 15 days.

Outdated text in the source. RA 9009 (2001) raised the income requirement for a component city to a locally generated average annual income of at least ₱100,000,000 for the last two consecutive years (2000 constant prices), plus either a contiguous territory of 100 square kilometers or a population of 150,000. A later amendment, as consolidated by one source, adds an alternative ₱400,000,000 threshold (2012 constant prices); confirm it against the official text before citing.
Section 30 does not appear in this source or in your PDF of CA 613; the numbering goes from Section 29 to Section 31.
The source reads “declared”; RA 386 reads “When the courts declare a law to be inconsistent with the Constitution”.
The text here correctly reads “situated”. Your uploaded Civil Code PDF reads “stipulated” at this point — that is a transcription error in that copy; the rule is lex situs.
The source drops “a” (“in manner”). RA 386 reads “in a manner that is contrary to morals, good customs or public policy”.
Source note normalised to lower case, as printed elsewhere in the Code.
De Leon prints “shall be held in abeyance”; the source reads “held in the abeyance”. Check your printed codal before memorising this phrase.
De Leon prints “The defense of illegality of contracts”; the source reads “contract”. Check your printed codal.
De Leon prints “As for obligations to do and not to do”; the source reads “As for the obligations”. The difference does not change the meaning.

The source shows the original Art. 2 (publication in the Official Gazette only). After Tañada v. Tuvera (1985–86), Executive Order No. 200 (1987) restated the rule so that laws take effect fifteen days after publication either in the Official Gazette or in a newspaper of general circulation.
The source shows Art. 39 as amended by E.O. 227 only. RA 8533 (1998) deleted the ten-year prescription for pre-Family Code marriages under Art. 36: the action now never prescribes.
The source shows the original Art. 176. RA 9255 (2004) allows an illegitimate child to use the father’s surname when the father has expressly recognized the child.
The source shows the original Art. 177. RA 9858 (2009) also allows legitimation when the parents’ only impediment at conception was that either or both were below eighteen.
The source shows the original Art. 234 (majority at twenty-one). RA 6809 (1989) lowered the age of majority to eighteen and removed emancipation by marriage or by recorded agreement.
The source shows the original Art. 236. RA 6809 (1989) rewrote it: parental consent is still needed to marry until twenty-one.
The source omits “only” (“enforced not within … but also outside”). The official text of Act No. 3815 reads “not only within the Philippine Archipelago … but also outside of its jurisdiction”.
The source drops “by” (“but also means of fault”). Restored to “but also by means of fault (culpa)”.

The text shown is the original 1930 article. As amended (Rep. Act No. 1978 and Batas Pambansa Blg. 873), Article 152 also defines agents of persons in authority (persons charged with maintaining public order and protecting life and property, such as barangay officials and police), treats teachers, professors and persons charged with the supervision of public or duly recognized private schools, colleges and universities, and lawyers in the actual performance of their professional duties or on the occasion of such performance, as persons in authority for the purposes of Articles 148 and 151, and deems any person who comes to the aid of persons in authority an agent of a person in authority. The amending texts are not in this library yet; read the article as amended before citing it.

The text shown is the original article. As amended, qualified theft is punished by the penalties next higher by two degrees, and the article also covers motor vehicles and mail matter, and property taken on the occasion of fire, earthquake, typhoon, volcanic eruption or any other calamity, vehicular accident or civil disturbance. Taking motor vehicles is now punished by RA 10883 (New Anti-Carnapping Act) and cattle rustling by PD 533. Read the article as amended before citing it.

The source shows Article 70 as originally enacted in 1930. Commonwealth Act No. 217 (1936) rewrote it, adding the three-fold rule and the 40-year limit; the text in force is shown under “Amended text”.
The source shows Article 71 as originally enacted (“Fine”). Commonwealth Act No. 217 (1936) replaced it with the graduated scales; the text in force is shown under “Amended text”.

The source shows the original Art. 39 (subsidiary liability for all pecuniary liabilities at a fixed peso rate). RA 5465 (1969) limited it to the fine; RA 10159 (2012) pegged it to the highest minimum wage. Two transcription typos (“fight felony”, “prision correctional”) are corrected.
Article 88-A was added by RA 11362, the Community Service Act (2019); the source predates it.

The source shows the original Art. 125. Executive Orders No. 59 (1986) and No. 272 (1987) set the periods now in force: 12, 18 and 36 hours according to the gravity of the offense. A transcription typo (“the caused of”) is corrected.
Article 134-A was added by RA 6968 (1990), which created the crime of coup d’état; the source predates it.
The source shows the original Art. 135 (rebellion and insurrection only). RA 6968 (1990) added coup d’état and its penalties.

The source shows the original Art. 177. RA 379 (1949) extended it to false representation as an officer, agent or representative of any department or agency of the government or of a foreign government.
The source shows the original Art. 270 (reclusion temporal). RA 18 (1946) raised the penalty to reclusion perpetua.
